content: Open redirect prevention: use allowlist (not blocklist) of trusted domains, parse URLs with built-in parsers (new URL()), reject protocol-relative URLs, decode fully before validation, always have a safe default. For URL shorteners specifically, redirect targets are inherently user-controlled by design (that's the product), so mitigation shifts to: scanning/reputation-checking target URLs at creation time, rate-limiting redirect creation, and not treating the shortener's own domain as a trusted redirect target for internal auth flows (e.g. OAuth callback allowlists must not include the shortener's redirect endpoint).
